purpose: Bend at hips, knees and ankles to lower the body under control to a chosen depth (ideally thighs about parallel or lower) with the trunk braced, knees tracking over the feet and weight balanced over mid-foot, then stand fully back up.

phases.description: From upright standing, hips and knees bend and hips lower under control until the lowest point.
Brief transition at the lowest position where the movement reverses.
Hips and knees extend, driving back up to full standing.

faults.description: Hips do not lower far enough; the squat stops well above thigh-parallel.
faults.cue_intent: Tell the person they are stopping short of a full squat and should sit lower.
faults.ask_if_unsure_intent: Ask whether they are deliberately doing a partial squat or if something limits going lower.
faults.fix_intent: Suggest sitting down and back further, possibly with a box or counterweight to feel the target depth, keeping heels down.

faults.description: The knee drifts inward toward the midline relative to the hip-ankle line during descent or bottom.
faults.cue_intent: Point out the knee collapsing inward and ask them to push the knees out over the toes.
faults.ask_if_unsure_intent: Ask whether they feel the knee falling inward or tension in the outer hip.
faults.fix_intent: Cue spreading the floor with the feet, pushing knees out in line with toes; consider a light resistance band or slightly reduced load/depth.

faults.description: Trunk tips far forward at the bottom, turning the squat into a hip hinge.
faults.cue_intent: Tell them the chest is dropping too far forward and ask them to keep the chest tall.
faults.ask_if_unsure_intent: Ask where they feel the effort and whether the heels or ankles feel tight.
faults.fix_intent: Cue chest up, knees travelling forward over toes, and a counterweight in front or heel elevation if ankle mobility limits.

faults.description: At the top the hips are not fully extended, leaving the person partly bent between reps.
faults.cue_intent: Mention they are not standing fully tall at the top.
faults.ask_if_unsure_intent: Ask whether they are keeping continuous tension deliberately between reps.
faults.fix_intent: Cue squeezing glutes and standing all the way up before starting the next rep.

outcomes.description: The squat pattern itself is performed with controlled, well-aligned technique.
Hips lower to about thigh-parallel or below.
Knees stay aligned over the feet throughout the rep.
Body weight stays balanced over the mid-foot with a stable trunk.
Rep starts and ends in full standing extension.

links.mechanism: A lower hip height at the bottom directly means greater squat depth.
Less inward knee deviation keeps the knee over the foot line.
Some forward lean counterbalances hips moving back, but too much shifts load away from an upright squat pattern.
More forward shin travel lets the hips go lower while the trunk stays more upright.
A more open hip angle at the top means full hip extension.
A stance around shoulder width suits most people's hip structure for reaching depth; very narrow or very wide limits it.

session_ideas: Set of 8-10 bodyweight squats filmed from the side, then from the front
Tempo squats: 3 seconds down, 1 second pause, quick up
Box squat to a target depth

vocabulary_proposals.name: height.hip_below_knee
vocabulary_proposals.why: Thigh-parallel depth is conventionally judged as hip crease relative to knee height; a direct hip-minus-knee vertical feature would be more exact than normalised hip height alone.

vocabulary_proposals.name: asymmetry.knee_angle_lr
vocabulary_proposals.why: Detecting a lateral shift or uneven squat needs a left-right difference in knee angle, which is not expressible with signed dom/non features.
